newsitem.title: UK: SmithKline says industry on dynamic threshold.
newsitem.headline: SmithKline says industry on dynamic threshold.

text.p: - SmithKline Beecham Plc's chairman of research and development George Poste said on Monday that the drugs industry was "on the threshold of the most dynamically productive time in the lifesciences of any time in human creativity."

In a speech to the FT World Pharmaceuticals Conference, Poste said that in recent years the world's top 20 drug companies had been producing new chemical entities at a rate of just one a year, a level which was "woefully inadequate for companies of that size and scale."
He said each new drug cost an average of $650 million on a fully-capitalized cost basis, and added that the move towards mega-mergers was "not a solution, it is buying time."

However, Poste said that with the expansion of genetic understanding, "the industry has gone from famine in terms of (disease) targets to absolute feast." The danger for the industry now was of moving, "from too few targets to too many," Poste said, adding that, "now the skill lies in the selection of targets to work on."

Poste said companies needed to develop a "fast in, fast out" approach to looking at disease targets, quickly abandoning those that did not look immediately promising, but ensuring they took out patent protection in case thay wanted to go back at a later date.

Poste said the day of the fully-integrated pharmaceutical company which did everything in-house was "dead," replaced by the "drumbeat of the importance of alliances." "This technology wave is far from over," Poste added.

He said drug companies now had to track developments in a whole range of new areas, including robotics, optics and lasers, computing, diagnostics and materials science, which was leading to changes in drug delivery mechanisms.
